overview: Two memos: in 1940 engineer Gano Dunn declined Mitsui's request for power-plant engineering help, backed informally by State, citing national-defense concerns; in 1943, neither Military Intelligence nor the Office of Economic Warfare wanted an old 1923 Toho Electric Power Company report.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation on Mitsui’s request for American engineering assistance
subfiles.about: Records Gano Dunn’s proposed refusal of Mitsui and Company’s request that the J. G. White Engineering Corporation help plan and erect hydraulic and steam power plants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gano Dunn tells State that Mitsui asked his firm to help build Japanese power plants; citing his National Defense Commission role, he proposed declining politely, and Ballantine and Mackay informally approved and thanked him.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on possible use of the Toho Electric Power Company report
subfiles.about: Records unsuccessful efforts to identify a wartime government use for a detailed 1923 report on the Toho Electric Power Company.
subfiles.summary: Memo notes Thomas sent Hornbeck a 1923 Toho Electric Power Company report; Military Intelligence had no need for it, and Economic Warfare's Butts found no interested recipient since it was prepared for a prior loan bid and copies already existed.

interest: Shows a 1940 U.S. firm declining to help Japan's power plants on defense grounds, and 1943 disinterest in a report.
